# Design: A merge that keeps a modified last requirement whole, and an update that refreshes its own skills

## Context

The merge is pure: `merge_into_existing` builds a list of byte-range
edits over the main spec, and `apply_edits` applies them sorted by
descending end, so that earlier offsets stay valid. Its comment assumes
that two edits never end at the same point. They do when a delta modifies
the section's last requirement — whose span runs to the end of the
section — and adds requirements, inserted at that same end: the stable
sort keeps the delta's order, the replacement goes first and lengthens the
text, and the insertion then lands at the old offset, inside the new text.
That is what cut `role-evaluation`'s last scenario at the archive of
`measure-consumption`.

`codev update` decides a skill was edited by hand when its content differs
from the rendering while carrying the running version's stamp. Between two
builds of one version — every build from source, codev's own repository —
the skill text changes and the stamp does not, so codev takes its own
earlier rendering for a hand edit.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**: compose a modification and an addition at the end of a section;
tell codev's renderings from hand edits whatever the version.

**Non-goals**: detecting a corrupted spec after the fact in `codev
validate` (the merge no longer produces one); repairing the
`role-evaluation` spec, which the change `evaluate-planning` restores
through its own delta.

## Decisions

### Decision: Ties between edits ending at one point put the insertion first

`apply_edits` sorts by descending end, then, for the same end, by
descending start: a zero-width insertion at `end` (start = end) is applied
before a replacement `start..end`, so the replacement no longer moves it.
Applied first, the insertion sits after `end`; the replacement of
`start..end` then rewrites only what lies before it. The comment that
called the case impossible is corrected.

**Alternatives considered**: inserting the added requirements after the
merge, on the merged text — a second pass that recomputes offsets the
plan already knows; forbidding a delta that modifies the last requirement
and adds one — a valid delta, refused.

### Decision: A skill carries the checksum of its own rendering

The rendering writes `checksum: "<sha256>"` under `metadata`, computed
over the whole skill without that line, with `codev_core::update::sha256_hex`
(the hashing codev already uses). The checksum decides only among skills stamped
with the running version: a skill stamped with another version is
rewritten, as before, so a hand edit never survives an upgrade and
`codev doctor` never meets a preserved skill it calls outdated. Among the
running version's skills, one whose content without the checksum line
hashes to the checksum is codev's and is rewritten; one that does not has
been edited and is preserved. A skill without the line was rendered
before checksums: it keeps today's rule — preserved unless it differs from
the rendering only by the review mode, compared with the checksum line
left out — so that no hand edit made before this change is overwritten
within its version.

**Alternatives considered**: a manifest of rendered hashes under
`_codev/` — a second file to keep in step and to commit; bumping the
version on every change of a skill — every build from source would still
meet the case.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A user edits a skill and also rewrites its checksum line] → They meant
  to make it codev's; `codev update` then rewrites it, as for any
  rendering.
- [The checksum line changes every skill once] → The first `codev update`
  after this release rewrites skills stamped with an earlier version, as
  it already does for any release. A project on a build from source with
  unchecksummed skills of the same version runs `codev update --force`
  once, as codev's own repository does in task 2.2.

# Proposal: A merge that keeps a modified last requirement whole, and an update that refreshes its own skills

## Why

Two defects found while dogfooding codev. Archiving the change
`measure-consumption` wrote its new requirement into the middle of a line
of the last requirement it modified, cutting a scenario of
`_codev/specs/role-evaluation/spec.md` in two — and `codev validate` let
it pass. And `codev update` left `codev-propose` and `codev-apply` stale,
calling them "edited by hand", whenever the skills' text changed without
a version change, as on every build from source: the fix needed `--force`,
which would also have erased real hand edits.

## What Changes

- A sync or an archive whose delta both modifies the main spec's last
  requirement and adds requirements writes the modified requirement whole,
  then the added ones after it.
- A rendered skill carries a checksum of its own content in its
  frontmatter (`metadata.checksum`). Among skills stamped with the
  running version, `codev update` rewrites one whose content still
  matches its checksum and preserves as edited by hand only one whose
  content no longer matches it; a skill stamped with another version is
  rewritten as today, and a skill rendered before checksums keeps today's
  rule.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- spec-merge
- skills

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- `crates/codev-core/src/merge/edits.rs` (the order of edits ending at
  the same point) and its tests in `merge/mod.rs`.
- `crates/codev-agents/src/claude.rs` (rendering with the checksum, the
  hand-edit decision); codev's own skills refreshed with `codev update`.
- Documentation: the FAQ (en and fr) on a spec cut by an earlier codev;
  the skill frontmatter in
  `docs/{en,fr}/src/reference/file-formats.md`, what `codev update`
  preserves in `docs/{en,fr}/src/reference/cli.md`, and the section on
  editing a generated skill in `docs/{en,fr}/src/skills.md`.

## Domains

- [ ] security
- [ ] personal-data
- [ ] user-interface
- [ ] performance
- [ ] operations
- [x] migration

## Release note

- Fixed: Archiving a change that modifies a spec's last requirement and adds requirements no longer cuts that requirement in two: the added ones are written after it.
- Fixed: `codev update` refreshes the skills it rendered itself even when their version stamp has not changed, and preserves only the skills edited by hand; each skill now carries a checksum of its content. Skills generated by an earlier codev are rewritten on upgrade as before; on a build from source, skills of the same version without a checksum are still preserved, and one `codev update --force` brings them under the checksum — check `git diff` first, since it also overwrites real hand edits.
- Fixed: Earlier codev versions could cut a spec's last requirement in two when one change both modified it and added requirements; `codev validate` does not detect it, and syncing again does not repair it. If you archived such a change, look at the spec it modified (the diff of the archive) and repair it by hand or with a new `MODIFIED` delta.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Frontmatter contract of a codev skill

Every skill shipped by codev MUST carry a valid YAML frontmatter whose
`name` matches the name of the `.claude/skills/<name>/` directory, whose
`allowed-tools` field includes at least `Bash(codev:*)`, and whose
`metadata.version` matches the version of the binary that generated it,
and whose `metadata.checksum` is the SHA-256, in hexadecimal, of the
skill's whole content with that `checksum` line left out. A skill whose
content no longer matches its checksum has been edited by hand.

#### Scenario: Frontmatter parsed by a third-party YAML reader

- **GIVEN** a skill shipped by the current version of the binary
- **WHEN** its frontmatter is extracted and passed to a standard YAML parser
- **THEN** the parser returns `name`, `allowed-tools`, `metadata.version`
  and `metadata.checksum` without error
- **AND** `metadata.version` equals the version the binary reports

#### Scenario: Hand edit detected on update

- **GIVEN** a skill whose body a user has edited by hand, without
  changing its version
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update` again without `--force`
- **THEN** the skill is not overwritten
- **AND** the update report flags it as preserved

#### Scenario: The checksum matches the content

- **GIVEN** a skill as the binary renders it
- **WHEN** the SHA-256 of its content without the `checksum` line is
  computed
- **THEN** it equals `metadata.checksum`

### Requirement: `codev update` regenerates the skills of the configured workflows

`codev update` SHALL write one skill per workflow listed by `workflows:` in
`_codev/config.yaml`, or per workflow of the default catalog when the key is
absent, at `.claude/skills/codev-<workflow>/SKILL.md`, rendered by the
running codev:

- a missing skill is created;
- a skill identical to the rendering is left untouched;
- a skill stamped with another codev version is rewritten;
- among the skills stamped with the running version, one whose content
  matches its own checksum is codev's rendering and is rewritten; one
  whose content no longer matches its checksum is edited by hand and is
  preserved; one without a checksum, rendered before checksums, is
  preserved as edited by hand unless it differs from codev's rendering
  only by the review mode, as the review-mode requirement says, the
  checksum line left out of the comparison;
- with `--force`, every skill is rewritten.

An unknown workflow name SHALL be ignored with a warning `unknown_workflow`
listing the workflows this codev provides; the other skills are written.
The skill of a workflow no longer listed SHALL be left in place: `codev
update` deletes no skill. `codev update` SHALL also recreate the missing
folders of `_codev/` and a missing `_codev/config.yaml`, without
overwriting any existing file. Its handling of codev's managed sections is
specified by the `init` capability. Outside a codev project it fails with
`no_codev_root` and writes nothing.

The human output SHALL start with `codev updated in <project root>`, list
the installed skills, then say how many files were created and updated, or
`Nothing to do, everything is already in place.`, and finally list the
preserved skills with a hint to rerun with `--force`. With `--json`, the
document SHALL carry `root`, `created`, `updated`, `untouched`,
`preserved`, `skills` (the names of the configured skills), `integration`
and `status` (warnings). The command exits with code 0.

#### Scenario: Missing and outdated skills are written

- **GIVEN** an initialized project whose `codev-explore` skill was deleted
  and whose `codev-sync` skill is stamped with an earlier codev version
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `created` lists the `codev-explore` skill and `updated` the
  `codev-sync` skill
- **AND** both carry the running codev's version stamp

#### Scenario: A second run changes nothing

- **GIVEN** a project where `codev update` just ran
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update`
- **THEN** `created` and `updated` are empty
- **AND** the human output says `Nothing to do, everything is already in
  place.`

#### Scenario: `--force` rewrites a hand-edited skill

- **GIVEN** a project whose `codev-apply` skill was edited by hand without
  changing its version stamp
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --force --json`
- **THEN** `updated` lists the `codev-apply` skill and `preserved` is empty
- **AND** the skill is back to what codev renders

#### Scenario: An unknown workflow is ignored with a warning

- **GIVEN** a configuration with `workflows: [propose, bogus]`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `skills` is `["codev-propose"]`
- **AND** `status` holds a warning `unknown_workflow` naming `bogus`

#### Scenario: A workflow removed from the configuration keeps its skill

- **GIVEN** a project where every default skill is installed, then
  `workflows: [propose]` in the configuration
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update`
- **THEN** `.claude/skills/codev-apply/SKILL.md` still exists, unchanged

#### Scenario: A deleted `_codev/` folder is recreated

- **GIVEN** an initialized project whose `_codev/specs/` folder was deleted
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `created` lists `_codev/specs/.gitkeep`
- **AND** `_codev/config.yaml` is listed in `untouched`, unchanged

#### Scenario: Outside a project

- **GIVEN** a folder with no `_codev/` in it or its parents
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1 and `status[0].code` is `no_codev_root`
- **AND** `root` is `null` and `skills` is empty

#### Scenario: A skill rendered by an earlier build of the same version

- **GIVEN** a project whose `codev-apply` skill was rendered by a build
  of the same version whose skill text differed, untouched since, with a
  `checksum` line matching its content
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `updated` lists the `codev-apply` skill and `preserved` is
  empty

#### Scenario: A hand edit of a checksummed skill

- **GIVEN** a project whose `codev-apply` skill a user edited by hand
  after codev rendered it with its checksum
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `preserved` lists the `codev-apply` skill, left as edited

#### Scenario: A hand edit survives no upgrade

- **GIVEN** a project whose `codev-apply` skill a user edited by hand,
  stamped with an earlier codev version
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json` with a newer codev
- **THEN** `updated` lists the `codev-apply` skill, as before checksums

#### Scenario: A skill rendered before checksums

- **GIVEN** a project whose `codev-apply` skill has no `checksum` line,
  is stamped with the running version and differs from its rendering
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev update --json`
- **THEN** `preserved` lists it, as before checksums existed

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Semantic merge per operation

A sync SHALL apply each operation of a delta according to its own
semantics: `ADDED` inserts at the end of the `## Requirements` section,
`MODIFIED` replaces the block of the requirement with the same name down to
the character, `REMOVED` deletes the entire block, `RENAMED` retitles only
the `### Requirement:` header without touching the body. The operations
SHALL compose: a requirement `ADDED` after a requirement that the same
delta modifies or renames lands after that requirement's whole new text,
never inside it, even when that requirement ends the section.

#### Scenario: ADDED appears at the end of Requirements

- **GIVEN** a main spec `user-auth` containing `## Requirements` with
  a requirement `Login`
- **AND** an `ADDED` delta carrying a requirement `Two-Factor Authentication`
  with its scenario
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the main spec now contains `Login` first, then
  `Two-Factor Authentication`
- **AND** the `Login` block — its header, its description, its scenarios —
  is identical down to the character to what it was

#### Scenario: MODIFIED replaces the requirement block without touching the others

- **GIVEN** a main spec containing two requirements `Login` and
  `Session Expiration`, in that order
- **AND** a `MODIFIED` delta carrying `Session Expiration` with a new
  scenario
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the `Session Expiration` block has been replaced by the delta's
  version
- **AND** the `Login` block and the whitespace separating the two
  requirements remain identical down to the character

#### Scenario: REMOVED deletes the entire requirement block

- **GIVEN** a main spec containing `Login` and `Remember Me`
- **AND** a `REMOVED` delta carrying `Remember Me`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the main spec no longer contains any trace of `Remember Me`
- **AND** the `Login` block remains identical down to the character

#### Scenario: RENAMED retitles the header and nothing else

- **GIVEN** a main spec containing `Session Expiration` with its
  scenarios
- **AND** a `RENAMED` delta mapping `Session Expiration` to `Session Timeout`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the requirement header has become `### Requirement: Session Timeout`
- **AND** the description and scenarios of that requirement are identical
  down to the character

#### Scenario: The last requirement modified and another added

- **GIVEN** a main spec whose `## Requirements` ends with `Login`
- **AND** a delta that modifies `Login`, making it longer, and adds
  `Export`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the main spec holds the delta's `Login` whole, then `Export`
- **AND** no line of `Login` is cut, and a second sync changes nothing

recommendation: |
  Give the helper a name that matches what it checks, and make the legacy branch read positively.

  The caller at lines 248-254 stores its result in a local called `edited_by_hand`, but only after two other tests: the content differs from `desired`, and the version stamp is the running version. So two things share one name, and the helper's answer is only true under conditions that live elsewhere. A reader who opens the helper alone sees `Some(checksum) => ... != checksum`, which ignores the version. They cannot tell whether a skill from an older version with a stale checksum counts as "edited by hand" without reading the doc comment's precondition and the caller.

  In the `None` branch, `.all(|ctx| current != ...)` means "matches none of the renderings". That double negative is easy to misread as "matches all of them". Building a two-element array with `self.ctx.clone()` just to iterate it adds more noise.

  Suggested fix:
